name: Wikipedia
goodFor: A lead paragraph and a picture for almost any term, and what a topic covers.
attribution: The article's title, linked to the article; the words "CC BY-SA 4.0", linked to https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/; and, when the text shown was shortened or changed, a note that it was.
access: https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/summary/{title} for an app; node tools/ref.mjs wikipedia "<title>" for an agent.

parts.name: Article text
parts.attribution: The article's title, linked to the article; the words "CC BY-SA 4.0", linked to https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/; and, when the text shown was shortened or changed, a note that it was.

evidence.quote: Permission is granted to copy, distribute and/or modify Wikipedia's text under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License
Text from external sources may attach additional attribution requirements to the work, which should be indicated on an article's face or on its talk page.

parts.notes: CC BY-SA 4.0 (also GFDL, which an app doesn't need). An article that carries a notice that text came from elsewhere may ask for more credit; keep that notice's credit with the text.

parts.name: Pictures and other files in articles

evidence.quote: Images on Wikipedia are not always covered by the same license as article text.
if you were using a Wikipedia article for a commercial use that would otherwise be allowed by our licenses and the doctrine of fair use, would not be allowed under that commercial use

parts.notes: Each file has its own licence on its description page, and some are non-free files used under US fair use, which a paid app can't rely on. The summary API's thumbnail is such a file. An app links to a picture until that file's own page is checked; see wikimedia-commons.

notes: Checked against Wikipedia:Copyrights and the Wikimedia Terms of Use. Article text is CC BY-SA 4.0, which allows commercial use, so a paid app may show an extract with the credit in attribution. Text that Ceder changes or adds to must itself be offered under CC BY-SA 4.0, and a shortened or changed extract carries a note that it was. Pictures don't share the text's licence (see parts). The Wikipedia name and logos are trademarks and aren't covered, so don't use the logo or suggest endorsement. The REST API is used under Wikimedia's API rules, which ask for a descriptive User-Agent. The bank is CC0 and can't carry share-alike text, so agents read a page to learn what a topic covers and never copy its wording (pipeline/prompts/sources.md). Articles often read above introductory level.
